problem: Prior single-task models for instruction following (semantic goal navigation) and embodied question answering, when trained jointly, overfit to the task in which a word was seen and fail to transfer word grounding across tasks (e.g. a word seen only in instructions is never used to answer questions).
motivation: Multi-task training could improve sample efficiency and let an agent generalize to unseen word compositions across tasks, e.g. follow 'Go to the red pillar' and answer 'What color is the torch?' after seeing those words in the other task only. This requires words in both input spaces and the answer space to be aligned with each other and grounded in visual feature maps.
key_idea: A Dual-Attention unit (Gated-Attention with bag-of-words, then Spatial-Attention, then Gated-Attention with a sentence embedding) aligns text words, convolutional feature channels and answer words in a task-invariant way, so knowledge transfers across SGN and EQA.
insight: Alignment is enforced by making every attention purely modulate the CNN feature maps, with the number of channels equal to the vocabulary size, so each channel becomes a word-specific detector; the visualizations show this alignment emerges even without auxiliary labels. The ablations show that Spatial-Attention and GA1 are essential (w/o SA: SGN 0.20/EQA 0.16 no aux), GA2 is critical for EQA but not SGN (w/o GA2 EQA 0.33 vs 0.53 no aux), and multitask training beats single-task (EQA 0.53 vs 0.31 no aux). Disentangled channels also make the model modular: appending external object detectors for new words gives good performance on unseen-word instructions.
method: Image encoder: 3-layer CNN producing V×H×W feature maps, with V set to the vocabulary size (union of instruction and question training vocabularies) so each channel corresponds to a word.
Text representations: a bag-of-words vector x_BoW and a GRU-based sentence embedding x_sent of dimension V.

Dual-Attention unit: GA1 (x_I gated by x_BoW) → sum over channels + softmax gives a spatial map x_spat → Spatial-Attention multiplies x_I by x_spat → GA2 with x_sent selects attribute types → sum over H,W + softmax gives the answer distribution x_Ans (answer space = vocabulary space).

Policy module: concatenates the flattened spatial attention map x_S with a time-step embedding and a task indicator, then applies a linear layer, a GRU and linear heads for policy and value; the answer is emitted via an answer action using argmax of x_Ans.
Optimization: PPO for the policy plus a supervised cross-entropy loss on answer prediction, with shared parameters; reward +1 for success, -0.001 per step, distance-based shaping for SGN.
Auxiliary task: predicts V×H×W spatial object/attribute presence labels directly on the conv output channels (no extra parameters) to keep the channel-word alignment.
Transfer to new words: train detectors for new words, resize to H×W, append as extra channels to x_I, and append the words to the BoW vector, with no fine-tuning of the policy.

setting.backbone: Custom small CNN + GRU + Dual-Attention + GRU policy (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: RL from scratch in ViZDoom: 70 instructions (42 train/28 test) and 29 questions (21 train/8 test); 10M frames (Easy), 50M frames (Hard); also House3D with 22+7 train items, 50M frames
setting.observation: egocentric RGB first-person image (3×168×300) plus text instruction or question
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward, left, right, plus an answer action
setting.privileged: none (auxiliary object/attribute labels used only in training; external object detectors assumed for the new-word transfer experiment)

numbers.extra: Easy setting, 10M frames, unseen-word test instructions/questions, distance reward shaping

numbers_note: Accuracies are on custom Doom/House3D unseen-word test sets, not standard navigation benchmarks; metric keys SGN_acc/EQA_acc are the paper's own. Training curves are only in figures. The new-word transfer results (Table 3, 0.68-1.00 on unseen-word instructions) are not listed above.
results: Dual-Attention reaches 86% SGN / 53% EQA on Easy without aux (96/58 with aux), versus the best baseline of about 33% on both tasks. On Hard with aux it gets 82% SGN / 59% EQA vs the best baselines 39% / 33% (Concat and Text only). It also transfers to unseen words via appended object detectors (0.68-1.00 accuracy).
limitations: Evaluated only in synthetic single-room ViZDoom (5 objects) and one House3D house, with a small vocabulary and templated language
Requires the vocabulary size to be fixed and channel-word alignment; new words need external object detectors, and fine-grained navigation complexity must stay consistent
Absolute EQA test accuracy stays modest (38-59%), and baselines were re-implemented by swapping in fusion modules
compares_to: Concat (Hermann et al. 2017 / Misra et al. 2017)
